arguments.title: Repair: Boundary Defects in Money Splitting, UTF-8 Labels and Local Days
arguments.spec:
# Boundary repair — three seeded, INDEPENDENT defects (project 60, repair_boundary_money_encoding_defects)

`src/` holds three tiny modules that are correct in the middle of their range and wrong at the edges:

- `src/money.mjs` `splitEvenly`: an even split of whole minor units that does not conserve the total — the shares
  must add up to exactly the total, every share a whole minor unit, no two shares differing by more than one, and
  the array must never increase from one share to the next (spare units go to the earliest shares).
- `src/label.mjs` `truncateForLabel`: a truncation that counts JavaScript string units where the hardware counts
  UTF-8 bytes — the result must never cut a character in half, must be a whole-character prefix, and must keep as
  many characters as fit the byte budget.
- `src/calendar.mjs` `localDayKey`: a calendar-day key that ignores the site's UTC offset, so it is only wrong near
  the day boundary — every instant inside one local day must answer with the same key even when the day straddles
  UTC midnight.

Repair the code only. Do not rewrite any module, do not change any exported name, and do not weaken the suite.
`scenarios/` and `test/` are FROZEN evidence, digest-checked on every run — never edit them, never add a dependency
(the sandbox is offline).

Some frozen scenarios are already green on the shipped tree, and they pass for the WRONG reason: the obvious
partial fix for money (floor every share, dump the whole remainder on the last share) and for label (slice the
encoded UTF-8 bytes, then decode) both make the currently-failing scenario pass while taking currently-green
sibling scenarios red with them (verified empirically: the naive money shape breaks split-shares-differ-by-at-most-one
and split-front-loads-the-remainder; a scenario that was passing must never go red). When a change turns a passing
scenario red, the change is the wrong shape — do not chase the scenario.

The deliverable is repair/manifest.json: `repaired` lists exactly the ids of the frozen scenarios that genuinely
pass right now; every id you list is executed on every run, so listing one that still fails takes the whole build
red with it. `complete: true` requires every scenario this fixture defines to be listed — reserved for the last
card.

How to plan this: one card per module, chained money -> label -> calendar (each depends on the previous so the
shared repair/manifest.json carries forward across isolated workspaces), then a final completeness card. Each fix
card lists that module's already-green scenario(s) in the manifest alongside its newly-fixed one(s), in the same
edit, so a shallow patch that turns a currently-green scenario red fails that same card's own npm test instead of
surviving to the end.

Acceptance check: npm test
arguments.plan:
Four-card chain, each depending on the previous so repair/manifest.json accumulates correctly across
isolated per-card workspaces:

1. fix-money-split-defect — repair src/money.mjs (root card).
2. fix-label-truncation-defect — repair src/label.mjs (depends on 1).
3. fix-calendar-offset-defect — repair src/calendar.mjs (depends on 2).
4. repair-completeness-verify-and-close — verify all 8 scenario ids pass and set complete: true (depends on 3).

Each of the three fix cards touches exactly one src/ module plus repair/manifest.json, and is scoped away from the
other two modules. The completeness card touches only repair/manifest.json. All four are declared not_testable:
test/** and scenarios/** are frozen and digest-checked, so no card can add a test file, and the acceptance is
running the fixture's own frozen npm test, not authoring a new one.

The three defects and their correct shapes were hand-verified against the real fixture in a scratch copy before
writing this plan (baseline: 5 of 8 scenarios fail; after the three fixes below: 8 of 8 pass; the two documented
shallow-fix traps were also reproduced and confirmed to break the currently-green scenarios they are expected to
break):
- money: base = floor(total/parts), remainder = total - base*parts, give one extra unit each to the FIRST
  `remainder` shares (not the last).
- label: walk `text` by character (`for...of`, which iterates by code point and never splits a surrogate pair),
  accumulate UTF-8 byte length via the existing `byteLength` helper, stop before exceeding maxBytes.
- calendar: `new Date(timestampMs + offsetMinutes * 60_000).toISOString().slice(0, 10)`.

tasks.title: Fix the money split's unit-conservation defect
tasks.prompt:
Fix the seeded boundary defect in src/money.mjs. `splitEvenly(totalMinor, parts)` currently does
`Math.round(totalMinor / parts)` for every share, so the shares do not add up to exactly totalMinor — for example
splitEvenly(1, 2) returns [1, 1], which sums to 2, not 1. Money is held in whole minor units and must never evaporate
and never appear from nowhere.

Baseline (verified against the real fixture): `split-sums-to-the-total` currently FAILS. Two siblings,
`split-shares-differ-by-at-most-one` and `split-front-loads-the-remainder`, currently PASS — but only by accident,
and this is the trap the specification warns about: the obvious partial fix (floor every share, then dump the whole
remainder onto the LAST share) makes `split-sums-to-the-total` pass but breaks BOTH currently-passing siblings
(confirmed: splitEvenly(2,3) under that shape spreads its shares by 2, and splitEvenly(1,2) puts the extra unit on
the last share instead of the first, so the array increases instead of staying front-loaded). A scenario that is
passing today must never go red because of your change — do not take that shape.

Correct shape: `base = Math.floor(totalMinor / parts)`, `remainder = totalMinor - base * parts`, and give exactly
one extra unit each to the FIRST `remainder` shares (not the last), leaving the rest at `base`. This sums to exactly
totalMinor, keeps every share a whole minor unit, keeps the spread between largest and smallest share at no more
than one, and keeps the array non-increasing (the spare units are front-loaded, so it never increases from one
share to the next).

Do not rewrite the module, do not change `splitEvenly`'s exported name or signature, and do not weaken the suite.
This is pure arithmetic — never add a dependency (the sandbox is offline).

fix described above. (3) In a further later turn, run npm test and confirm all three money scenarios now pass:
split-sums-to-the-total, split-shares-differ-by-at-most-one, split-front-loads-the-remainder. (4) In a final later
turn, read repair/manifest.json fresh and edit it to list all three of those ids in `repaired` (schemaVersion stays
1, complete stays false), re-read to confirm, then run npm test once more (never in the same turn as an edit) to
confirm it is still green with all three ids executing successfully.

tasks.title: Fix the label truncation's UTF-8 byte-counting defect
tasks.prompt:
Fix the seeded boundary defect in src/label.mjs. `truncateForLabel(text, maxBytes)` currently does
`text.slice(0, maxBytes)`, which counts JavaScript string units (UTF-16 code units), not the UTF-8 bytes the
hardware actually counts. This both over- and under-counts for any non-ASCII text, and for an astral character
stored as a surrogate pair (e.g. the emoji in this fixture's labels) it can cut a character in half.

Baseline (verified against the real fixture): `a-label-that-already-fits-is-untouched` currently PASSES (a slice
long enough to cover the whole string returns the whole string either way). `a-label-fits-its-byte-budget` and
`a-label-never-splits-a-character` currently FAIL. This has the same trap shape as the money module: the obvious
partial fix (encode the whole string to UTF-8 bytes, slice the byte array at maxBytes, decode back) does not
correctly solve it either — decoding a byte slice that lands inside a multi-byte character does not reliably
reconstruct a clean whole-character prefix. Do not take that shape.

Correct shape: iterate `text` by character (`for (const character of text)` iterates by Unicode code point and
never splits a surrogate pair), accumulate each character's UTF-8 byte length using the existing `byteLength`
helper, and stop BEFORE adding a character that would push the running total over `maxBytes`. Return the characters
kept so far, joined back into a string. This never cuts a character in half, is always a whole-character prefix of
the input, never exceeds the byte budget, and returns text untouched when it already fits.

Do not rewrite the module, do not change `truncateForLabel` or `byteLength`'s exported names or signatures, and do
not weaken the suite. Never add a dependency (the sandbox is offline) — `TextEncoder`/`TextDecoder` are already
imported; nothing else is needed.

tasks.title: Fix the calendar day-key's UTC-offset defect
tasks.prompt:
Fix the seeded boundary defect in src/calendar.mjs. `localDayKey(timestampMs, offsetMinutes)`
currently ignores `offsetMinutes` entirely and returns the UTC calendar day. Baseline (verified against the real
fixture): both frozen calendar scenarios currently FAIL — `the-day-key-follows-the-local-offset` and
`the-day-key-is-constant-inside-a-local-day`. Unlike the other two modules there is no accidental-pass trap here;
neither scenario passes today.

`offsetMinutes` is minutes EAST of UTC (330 for +05:30, -300 for -05:00). Correct shape: shift the timestamp by the
offset before reading the UTC calendar day — `new Date(timestampMs + offsetMinutes * 60_000).toISOString().slice(0,
10)`. Adding the eastward offset converts a UTC instant into the site's local wall-clock instant; that instant's UTC
day key is the local day key. This makes the instant of local midnight begin the new day, keeps the millisecond
before it in the day that is ending, and keeps every instant inside one local day answering with the same key even
when the day straddles UTC midnight — exactly what both frozen scenarios check, across all eight offsets in the
fixture including the fractional-hour ones (+05:30, +05:45, -11:00, +09:30).

Do not rewrite the module, do not change `localDayKey`'s exported name or signature, and do not weaken the suite.
Never add a dependency (the sandbox is offline) — no date library is needed or allowed.
